title: Looking for testers for a cloud platform for building games
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
I've been a long time follower and creator of games using ai and a software engineer as my primary career. For the past 6 months, I've been building pieces of a platform that allows people to build games on a few different engines: unity, godot, threejs, and pulse (a WIP custom engine) in the cloud.

The overarching goal I had was to define a very clear workflow for creating higher fidelity/cohesive proof of concept games and allow these to be created without needing specialized libraries/software.   
  
**A few motivations:**  
\- Many of the existing tooling does not allow multiple game engines  
\- google's playground service produces pure slop along with most other "similar' services  
\- I've been building games for one of my friends kids, and there was simply no way to give them a way to add onto it without spending hours setting it up. I moved the unity game I created for him to the platform.  
\- Nit together asset generation, design tools (like blender), and game engines into a cohesive product.  
\- provide access to my own local coding agent via MCP, so that I can leverage the cloud server, but have my own agent iterate on code to save on llm api costs.

I'm looking for up to 2-3 testers to give it a try on some game ideas: [https://gamecrew.ai/](https://gamecrew.ai/)  
And provide feedback. The demo video there is out of date, the platform is much improved from that state. Testing is free, but limited. Feel free to request access on the site, or DM me. 

It is a WIP but does work quite well on the three core engines. The Pulse engine is very experimental but the goal is that there needs to be a game engine built from the ground up for agents. There are a ton of inefficiencies with existing engines since they are designed for human maintenance. 

Long term goal would be to add more cutting edge tooling as the field develops (such as [https://xxxx0601.github.io/trig/](https://xxxx0601.github.io/trig/) ) -- and in addition I would love for it to be significantly faster.
